description: Use when someone asks how many commits are mine across all my email addresses, how much of this repo is my work, what did my Claude Code usage deliver, a summary of exported Claude Code session logs (token totals, per-model and tool counts, co-authored commits), whether this report or these files can be trusted, or to tailor my resume or CV to a job description. Covers proof of my work, CV or résumé bullets, a promotion or performance self-review paragraph, a visa or immigration evidence pack, a portfolio entry, work from a private repo they cannot share, a Claude Code usage or impact report for my manager, commits under several email addresses, three different email addresses or an old work email, and a workproof-report.json or files someone sent as evidence. Runs the workproof CLI (npx workproof, check, verify, sessions, verdict, bullets) or reads the user's own portfolio bank or past resume, instead of counting by hand. Numbers come from a report with a hash and no source code.
---

# workproof

Turns a git repository, including a private one, into a report of one author's work. The report has no source code, no file paths and no email addresses by default, and carries a hash a reader can check. Every figure prints the git command behind it and what it cannot show.

Requirements: Node 22 or newer, and git.

## Start here

- The person names a folder of exported Claude Code sessions, or asks for token totals, per-model counts or tool counts:

# My work in fx

- Commits: 63 non-merge commits are mine, out of 131 non-merge commits by everyone between my first and my last commit (2013-11-07 to 2015-08-22).
- Surviving lines: 697 of the 1,417 lines at HEAD are mine (49.2%), counted with git blame -w -M.

## Which addresses are counted

Addresses counted in total: 3 (the configured one, any address whose commits carry the same name, and those merged by rule).

Counted as the same person: 1 other address, because the rules matched: a GitHub noreply address whose login matches the name or the address in git config. This is a rule, not proof: it can be wrong, and --no-merge-identities counts only the configured address and addresses with the same name.

## What this does not show

Commits measure activity and surviving lines measure what lasted; neither measures quality, review or design. Run `npx workproof` and `npx workproof verify` for a report a reader can check.
usage: workproof [options] [--repo <dir>]...
       workproof check <report.json> [--countersign <file.dsse.json>]... [--allowed-signers <file>]
       workproof countersign <report.json> --key <ssh-key> [--repo <dir>] [--fingerprint-key <hex>] [--as <label>]
       workproof verify <report.json> [--repo <dir>]... [--fingerprint-key <hex>]
       workproof verdict <report.json> [--repo <dir>]... [--author <name|email>]... [--fingerprint-key <hex>] [--out <file>]
                 a verdict on a report someone else sent, checked against the repository it names
